source: Written by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from the county counts (AP via The New York Times), the 2024 baseline and Census ACS 2023 context.

40037.t:
Creek County stayed firmly Republican in the U.S. Senate race but moved 14 points toward the Democrats. Hern beat Thomas 14,357 to 5,637, a margin of 42 points, down from Trump's 56-point win in 2024. That shift is close to the typical Oklahoma county (+13) and the typical county nationally (+14), and every one of the state's 77 counties moved left. Among similar counties, Rogers moved 14 points, Garfield 12 and Carter 18. Statewide, Hern won by 18 points after Trump's 34.

Turnout was far lower. Creek cast 20,717 votes, about two-thirds of its 31,312 in 2024. So the count cannot show how much of the move came from voters changing their minds and how much from who stayed home.

40017.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Republican Kevin Hern carried Canadian County over Democrat N'Kiyla Thomas by 31,509 votes to 20,725, a margin of 20 points. Trump had won it by 40 in 2024, so the county moved 21 points toward the Democrats. That was the second-largest move among Oklahoma's 77 counties, every one of which moved left. The typical county moved 13 points and the state as a whole 16.

Turnout was 54,217, about 74% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among counties of similar size and 2024 lean, Muskogee moved 18 points, Okmulgee 16 and Osage 14.

Woodward's shift was slightly smaller than the typical county's 13 points and the state's 16, ranking 52nd of 77. Similar counties moved by similar amounts: Kingfisher by 11 points, Beckham by 12 and Atoka by 13.

Turnout fell sharply. About 4,740 votes were cast, 65% of the 2024 total of 7,312. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell whether the shift came from people changing their minds or from some voters staying home.
